mixos-mcp

mixos-mcp is an MCP stdio server for agents. Install the binary at <prefix>/bin/mixos-mcp and register the MCP server as mixos. It ships in the server prefix archive. Its package, binary and component are the single naming exception.

Connection

The server starts without a Bus connection. The first Bus tool connects using libs/bus. MIXOS_NODED_URL overrides the node configuration URL; otherwise the native client's node config discovery applies, including MIXOS_NODE_CONFIG, MIXOS_ETC and the user/system defaults.

Set MIXOS_BROKER_ACCOUNT to the broker's operating-system account and MIXOS_BUS_SOCKET to the session's Unix socket when overriding discovery. The account order is MIXOS_BROKER_ACCOUNT, node.conf noded.account, then noded; socket ownership never selects the trusted account.

Unix candidates are tried in order: explicit MIXOS_BUS_SOCKET, node.conf noded.unix_socket, this environment's <run>/noded/bus.sock, the system <run>/noded/bus.sock, then the endpoint advertised by noded.ping at the resolved URL. Only missing path components are skipped, with a warning. An existing candidate must pass path, account, peer-credential and protocol verification; any failure is fatal. A server-PID pin forbids skipping and ping.

Candidates are captured before connection. An unpinned client retries once if a selected path disappears; a second disappearance follows the missing-candidates policy below. Socket and account overrides are independent, so broken lower-priority node settings cannot veto an explicit override.

Verified Unix ingress is required whenever any candidate exists. When all candidates are missing, plain TCP requires MIXOS_MCP_ALLOW_TCP=1; the default is to refuse it and list the candidates tried. Calls are never replayed after reconnecting.

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mixos": {
      "command": "<prefix>/bin/mixos-mcp",
      "env": {
        "MIXOS_NODED_URL": "ws://192.0.2.10:4200/ws",
        "MIXOS_BROKER_ACCOUNT": "user",
        "MIXOS_BUS_SOCKET": "<runtime>/session/4/noded/bus.sock"
      }
    }
  }
}

Tools

Each name below is exposed as mcp__mixos__<name> in Claude Code.

  • bus_call, bus_list_services, bus_node_info, bus_list_peers, noded_ping (bus_list_peers leaves retired mesh members out unless include_retired: true)
  • term_list, term_snapshot, term_type, term_tab, term_pane
  • log_tail, log_search
  • app_describe, app_actions, app_execute
  • desktop_windows, desktop_window_wait
  • clipboard_get, clipboard_set
  • context_search, index_workspace, knowledge_digest
  • docs_feedback, journal_feedback, memory_feedback, journal_supersede
  • mix_execute, mcp_status

clipboard_get {selection?, mime?, primary?, offset?} and clipboard_set {text, selection?, mime?, primary?, sensitive?} use the local clipd. Selection is clipboard or primary; primary remains an alias. Reads return encoding and continuation fields, or a blobd reference for binary/large content. See clipd for limits and cross-session push semantics.

Application commands

app_describe {service} calls app.describe on that Bus service. app_actions {service} calls <service>.actions. Its result contains the application's command rows unchanged: id, label, menu, shortcut, more (when present), enabled and checked, plus any further metadata.

app_execute {service, id, params?} calls <service>.execute once with {id} or {id, params}. service is a Bus service name such as "workshop", id is a dotted command id such as "file.refresh", and params is an optional JSON object. Parameters are forwarded unchanged as a sibling of id; the application owns validation and may refuse unsupported parameters. Successful calls return {service, command, result}; application error messages from the Bus client pass through unchanged as tool errors. The same error-text pass-through and prefix removal apply to app_describe, desktop_windows and desktop_window_wait through their shared native helper.

Retired tools: app_actions_list, app_action_invoke, app_controls_list, app_control_get, app_control_set and app_control_wait have been removed without aliases. Use app_actions and app_execute for registry commands, and app_describe to discover an application's state commands. These retired tool names must not be reused.

Knowledge tools

context_search returns documents, journals, specs, plans, notes, memory, source comments, observations and scripts, grouped by source. It applies source trust weights and journal age limits. index_workspace indexes workspace content. knowledge_digest {} returns global index statistics under statistics and bounded staleness samples under stale, including legacy rows. It explicitly queries chunks never retrieved for 90 days, low-value chunks retrieved more than 3 times, and chunks dormant for 180 days, with 5 samples per bucket. If the stale query fails, statistics remain available, stale is null and stale_error contains the failure message (otherwise it is null). The optional domain argument is recognised but any non-null value is refused before connecting: indexd's stats and stale APIs cannot filter by domain. Omit domain for a global digest; it is never silently ignored or inferred. These tools send indexd.<action> requests to the configured indexd transport. An absent backend returns an explicit tool error. Settings are MixOS strict-data files: knowledge.conf.mix and domains.conf.mix.

The knowledge skills loop was retired on 2026-10-27. The six skills_* tools, knowledge_brief, skill refinement and graduation to CLAUDE.md are removed without aliases. context_search neither queries skills nor returns a skills group. Existing stored skills remain untouched; these retired tool names must not be reused. The server no longer instructs clients to capture, refine or rate knowledge after tasks.

At deployment, remove trust_weight_graduated and trust_weight_skill from knowledge.conf.mix, along with any old skills or llm sections there. Remove the retired skills.conf.mix and llm.conf.mix files from the MCP configuration directory ($MIXOS_ETC, normally ~/.config/mixos). They are no longer read or generated. No compatibility aliases are provided. The config::store::load_service loader tolerates unknown keys for KnowledgeSettings: the retired keys are ignored, not rejected. A fixture test exercises its directory-explicit core with those keys and invalid retired files, and verifies that generated defaults omit them. Existing config files are not rewritten; the coordinator removes the obsolete entries at deployment.

The optional docs_feedback, journal_feedback and memory_feedback tools remain because indexd consumes their scores when ranking search results and selecting low-value staleness candidates. journal_supersede hides an obsolete chunk while retaining it for audit. To purge old CMM observations, use the existing indexd filtered delete.

Host indexd from a desk

When a desk cannot reach the host's Bus, select SSH in $MIXOS_ETC/knowledge.conf.mix (normally ~/.config/mixos/knowledge.conf.mix):

indexd: {
    transport: "ssh",
    target: "indexd",
    ssh_host: "user@host.example",
    ssh_command: ["<prefix>/bin/indexd", "bridge"],
    call_timeout_secs: 120
}

Install indexd on the host and configure key-based SSH access for the desk's user. The client runs ssh -T -o BatchMode=yes -o ServerAliveInterval=30 with the configured host and command. The host command runs in the remote login shell; use trusted command arguments. indexd bridge uses the host's local Bus; target selects the address only in Bus mode.

One bridge is shared by knowledge tools for the MCP server's lifetime, with one request in flight at a time. Each call has a deadline, including queueing and retries. A broken pipe, exited child or bridge transport failure gets one restart and retry; an application error is returned immediately. A timeout discards the child and returns an error without replaying the call. A retried mutation may already have executed, so retry is not an exactly-once guarantee. Normal MCP shutdown closes stdin and reaps the bridge. Restart the MCP server after changing transport settings.

Missing settings default to transport: "bus", target: "indexd", the command above, an empty ssh_host and a 120-second call deadline. SSH mode requires ssh_host. When a Bus route is available, select transport: "bus", target: "indexd.host.example.bus" instead. Presence is checked with indexd.stats at the configured target, including routed targets.

The default client domain map expands the user's home for ~/Projects/mixos (mixos), ~/.mix (mix), ~/.ns (ns) and ~/.mc (mc). Custom domains.conf.mix maps override these defaults. index_workspace expands only a leading ~ or ~/, resolves the workspace to an absolute path, and sends absolute file paths and content to indexd.

Terminal tools preserve explicit pane selection and instance checks. Native application tools require an exact service and semantic target. Read-only tools do not invoke mutations; arbitrary bus_call and mix_execute can. Mix execution runs in an isolated worker with bounded output.

Logging and tests

Stdout is reserved for MCP. Logs go to stderr, journald and ~/.local/log/mixos/mixos-mcp.log. Arguments and results are redacted by default; RUST_LOG=mixos_mcp=trace explicitly enables full arguments. --version --json reports build provenance without starting MCP or the Bus.

Package tests cover parameter translation, target guards, output schemas, redaction and retirement of the skills protocol. The stdio integration test uses the real fixture broker, including verified Unix ingress and lazy reconnection. An in-process fake application checks command listing, execute request bodies with and without parameters, and unchanged application error messages. It also checks configured knowledge targets, paginated re-indexing and absolute file metadata. SSH client tests use a local Mix fake bridge through a test-only command hook; no SSH connection or indexd process is required.
